pairs: you who follow what is just
attendite ad petram unde excisi estis,
Pay attention to the rock from which you have been hewn,
et ad cavernam laci de qua præcisi estis.
and to the walls of the pit from which you have been dug.
Therefore, the Lord will console Zion,
and he will console all its ruins.
et ponet desertum ejus quasi delicias,
And he will turn her desert into a place of delights,
et solitudinem ejus quasi hortum Domini.
and her wilderness into a garden of the Lord.
Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea,
Gladness and rejoicing will be found in her,
thanksgiving and a voice of praise.
For a law will go forth from me,
et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet.
and my judgment will rest as a light for the nations.
And my arms will judge the people.
The islands will hope in me,
and they will patiently wait for my arm.
Lift up your eyes to heaven,
and look down to the earth below.
For the heavens will vanish like smoke,
and the earth will be worn away like a garment,
et habitatores ejus sicut hæc interibunt:
and its inhabitants will pass away in like manner.
salus autem mea in sempiternum erit,
But my salvation will be forever,
and my justice will not fail.
you who know what is just,
populus meus, lex mea in corde eorum:
my people who have my law in their heart.
Do not be afraid of disgrace among men,
and do not dread their blasphemies.
sicut enim vestimentum, sic comedet eos vermis,
For the worm will consume them like a garment,
et sicut lanam, sic devorabit eos tinea:
and the moth will devour them like wool.
salus autem mea in sempiternum erit,
But my salvation will be forever,
et justitia mea in generationes generationum.
and my justice will be from generation to generation.
Rise up as in the days of antiquity,
Have you not struck the arrogant one
Have not you dried up the sea,
the waters of the great abyss,
and turned the depths of the sea into a road,
so that the delivered could cross over it?
Et nunc qui redempti sunt a Domino, revertentur,
And now, those who have been redeemed by the Lord will return.
And they will arrive in Zion, praising.
et lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum:
And everlasting rejoicing will be upon their heads.
They will take hold of gladness and rejoicing.
Anguish and mourning will flee away.
I myself, who will console you.
Quis tu, ut timeres ab homine mortali,
Who are you that you would be afraid of a mortal man,
et a filio hominis qui quasi fœnum ita arescet?
and of a son of man, who will wither like the grass?
Et oblitus es Domini, factoris tui,
And have you forgotten the Lord, your Maker,
qui tetendit cælos et fundavit terram;
who extended the heavens, and who founded the earth?
et formidasti jugiter tota die a facie furoris ejus qui te tribulabat,
And have you been in constant dread, all day long, at the face of his fury,
et paraverat ad perdendum. Ubi nunc est furor tribulantis?
of the one who afflicted you and who had prepared to destroy you? Where is the fury of the oppressor now?
Advancing quickly, he will arrive to be revealed,
et non interficiet usque ad internecionem,
and he will not kill unto utter destruction,
Ego autem sum Dominus Deus tuus,
But I am the Lord, your God,
and who makes the waves swell.
The Lord of hosts is my name.
Posui verba mea in ore tuo,
I have placed my words in your mouth,
et in umbra manus meæ protexi te,
and I have protected you in the shadow of my hand,
so that you might plant the heavens,
and so that you might say to Zion,
quæ bibisti de manu Domini calicem iræ ejus;
from the hand of the Lord, the cup of his wrath.
usque ad fundum calicis soporis bibisti,
You drank, even to the bottom of the cup of deep sleep.
And you were given to drink, all the way to the dregs.
There is no one who can uphold her,
out of all the sons whom she has conceived.
et non est qui apprehendat manum ejus,
And there is no one who would take her by the hand,
out of all the sons whom she has raised.
There are two things which have happened to you.
Who will be saddened over you?
Your sons have been cast out.
dormierunt in capite omnium viarum sicut oryx illaqueatus,
They have slept at the head of all the roads, and they have been ensnared like a gazelle.
pleni indignatione Domini, increpatione Dei tui.
They have been filled by the indignation of the Lord, by the rebuke of your God.
and you who have been inebriated, but not by wine.
Thus says your Sovereign, the Lord,
who will fight on behalf of his people:
Ecce tuli de manu tua calicem soporis,
Behold, I have taken the cup of deep sleep from your hand.
fundum calicis indignationis meæ: non adjicies ut bibas illum ultra.
You shall no longer drink from the bottom of the cup of my indignation.
Et ponam illum in manu eorum qui te humiliaverunt,
And I will set it in the hand of those who have humiliated you,
and who have said to your soul:
et posuisti ut terram corpus tuum,
And you placed your body on the ground,
as a path for them to pass over.
